denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CMG 0104 (inpatient rehabilitation facility admission, stroke) with dates of service 2026-07-25 through 2026-08-08. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: Documentation does not demonstrate that the member required the intensity of services provided in an inpatient rehabilitation facility; the member’s needs could have been met at a skilled nursing facility level of care.

criteria.text: Requires active and ongoing intervention of at least two therapy disciplines, one of which is physical or occupational therapy.
Requires, and can reasonably be expected to actively participate in, an intensive rehabilitation program: generally at least 3 hours of therapy per day at least 5 days per week.
Reasonably expected to make measurable functional improvement of practical value within a prescribed period, documented against goals in an individualized plan of care.
Requires supervision by a rehabilitation physician with face-to-face visits at least 3 days per week to manage medical and rehabilitation needs.
The patient’s needs cannot be met at a less intensive level of care, such as a skilled nursing facility.

chart.text: Preadmission screening. 71 year old man with an acute left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke 6 days ago, NIHSS 10, dense right hemiparesis, right neglect, and oropharyngeal dysphagia on a modified diet. Needs PT for transfers and gait, OT for right upper extremity and self-care, and SLP for swallowing and cognition. Premorbidly independent, lives with his spouse in a single-level home. A skilled nursing facility would not provide the daily physician oversight he needs for the blood pressure lability and the dysphagia, nor three disciplines at this intensity. Recommend inpatient rehabilitation.

Admitted to inpatient rehabilitation from the acute hospital. History otherwise hypertension, hyperlipidemia, remote smoking history. Medications reconciled. Code status full. Post-admission physician evaluation. Confirms the preadmission findings. Three disciplines ordered: PT, OT, and SLP, each to evaluate within 24 hours. Prognosis for functional gains is good given premorbid independence and intact comprehension. Goals in 14 days: supervision level transfers, 150 feet with a hemi-walker, modified independent feeding, regular diet with thin liquids.
PT evaluation. Transfers maximal assist of two, sit to stand with right knee buckling, unable to ambulate. Sitting balance fair, standing balance poor. Goals set, plan 5 to 6 days a week.
OT evaluation. right upper extremity flaccid with trace shoulder shrug, dependent for dressing and bathing, maximal assist for grooming, right neglect on cancellation testing. Goals set.

SLP evaluation. Oropharyngeal dysphagia with delayed swallow and throat clearing on thin liquids, mechanical soft and nectar thick recommended. Mild word-finding difficulty, follows two-step commands. Goals set.

Rehab physician progress note, day 1, seen face to face. Reviewed the acute hospital course and the therapy evaluations, confirmed goals with the team. Blood pressure 158 over 90. Dysphagia precautions reinforced.
Fall risk assessment completed, score 41, high risk. Bed alarm on, nonskid socks, call light within reach, hourly rounding. Family at bedside this evening.
Rehab physician progress note, day 2, seen face to face. Tolerated the first full therapy day. Mild orthostatic drop in the gym, fluids encouraged. Bowel and bladder program started.
IV site rotated from the left forearm to the right hand, old site without redness. Dressing dated. Patient tolerated well.

Rehab physician progress note, day 3, seen face to face. Blood pressure labile, 168 over 94 this morning, 112 over 70 last night with lightheadedness in therapy; adjusted the amlodipine timing. Dysphagia diet reviewed with SLP. right shoulder pain with range of motion, added a sling for transfers.
Bowel regimen started, senna and docusate at bedtime. Last bowel movement 2 days ago per patient. Encouraged fluids and ambulation as able.
Dentures labeled and placed in the denture cup at the bedside. Patient prefers them out at night. Oral care done.
Patient requested something for sleep. Melatonin 3 milligrams given per order at 2130. Slept in two-hour stretches per night shift report.

Rehab physician progress note, day 5, seen face to face. Blood pressure 142 over 84 on the adjusted schedule, no further lightheadedness in therapy. Shoulder pain better with the sling. Swallow advancing per SLP.
Skin assessment on admission. Braden 18. Skin intact, no pressure injury, heels floated. Turn every two hours while in bed. Barrier cream to the sacrum as a precaution.
Glucose checks before meals and at bedtime, ranging 149 to 202. Sliding scale given per protocol. Patient's own glucometer at bedside, sent home with family for safekeeping.
Daily weight 149 pounds, up 0 from yesterday. Intake and output recorded. Repositioned per schedule, skin checked.

Team conference, day 7. Transfers improved from maximal assist of two to minimal assist of one. Gait 25 feet to 80 feet with a hemi-walker and contact guard. Swallow advanced to mechanical soft with nectar liquids. On track for the 14 day goals, continue.
Dietitian consult. Regular diet with heart healthy modification. Intake about 67 percent of meals. Supplement shake twice daily added. Will follow.
Audiology screen at nursing's request. He wears a hearing aid on the right, battery replaced, hears conversational voice well now. No further needs.
Rehab physician progress note, day 9, seen face to face. Afebrile, voiding, bladder scan residuals 80 and 110. Mood good, sleeping. Discussed the discharge target with him and the family.
Social work met with the patient and his daughter to confirm the home address, the primary contact, and transportation for follow-up appointments. No barriers identified today.

Rehab physician progress note, day 10, seen face to face. Blood pressure steadier on the new schedule. Bladder scan residuals under 100, catheter out. Spasticity in the right hand, started a night splint. Reviewed therapy progress with the team.
Pharmacy note. Renal dosing reviewed, creatinine 1.2, no adjustments needed today. Home medication list reconciled with the daughter by phone, one duplicate statin removed.
Potassium 3.4 this morning, repleted with 20 milliequivalents oral per protocol. Recheck with morning labs.
Rehab physician progress note, day 12, seen face to face. Medically stable, home medications finalized, home health orders written. Three physician visits this week documented.

Discharge summary, day 14. Transfers supervision, ambulating 160 feet with a hemi-walker and supervision, regular diet with thin liquids, feeding modified independent. Home with spouse, home health PT and OT arranged.
Home levothyroxine resumed at the home dose this morning after review with the attending. No interactions flagged.
Pneumococcal vaccine status reviewed, up to date per state registry. Influenza vaccine offered and accepted, given left deltoid.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-2 (intensity); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
